title: Automated Lipid Bilayer Membrane Formation Using a Polydimethylsiloxane Thin Film
protocol: Dissolve 1 M KCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl, and 1 mM EDTA in distilled water to formulate buffer solution.
Adjust pH of the buffer solution to 8.0.
Filter the buffer solution using a 0.20 μm filter.
Autoclave the filtered buffer solution at 121 °C for 15 min.
Dissolve 3% DPhPC lipid in a mixture of 2:8 n-decane and hexadecane to formulate lipid solution for pre-painting.
Stir the lipid solution overnight using a rotator.
Dissolve 0.1% DPhPC lipid in a mixture of 2:8 squalene and hexadecane to formulate lipid solution for membrane formation.
Stir the lipid solution overnight using a rotator.
Mix PDMS and curing agent in a 9:1 (w/w) ratio to form the PDMS prepolymer.
Add 5 g of PDMS prepolymer to a Petri dish to form the PDMS thin film (thickness 200 - 250 μm).
Spread PDMS pre-polymer using a spin coater at 800 rpm for 10 sec to form a thin film.
Place the Petri dish into a vacuum desiccator at a pressure of 100 mTorr for 2 hr to remove air bubbles.
Bake the Petri dish in an oven for 5 hr at 70 °C to polymerize the pre-polymer thin film.
Cut the polymerized PDMS thin film into 2 x 2 cm² squares.
Use a 500 µm micro punch to make an aperture in the center of the PDMS thin film.
Pre-paint apertures with 3% DPhPC lipid solution mixed in 2:8 n-decane and hexadecane.
Design two symmetric blocks of the chamber using 3D drawing software.
Craft the chamber using a PTFE block with a CNC machine following manufacturer's instructions.
Place the pre-painted PDMS thin film between the two PTFE blocks such that the aperture on the PDMS thin film is aligned with the hole in the chamber.
Seal the outer edges of the chamber using a cover glass with grease for optical observation.
Immobilize the assembled chamber using nuts and bolts.
Deposit 0.5 µl of 0.1% DPhPC lipid mixed in 2:8 n-decane:hexadecane onto the aperture of the PDMS thin film.
Store the chamber in a freezer or refrigerator below 10 °C prior to use.
Suspend 2 ml of buffer solution in each side of the chamber for BLM formation.
Place the chamber onto a micromanipulator to control elevation precisely.
Illuminate one side of the chamber using a halogen fiber optic illuminator.
Observe BLM formation on the other side with a digital microscope magnified by 200X.
Confirm BLM formation when the center of the aperture appears brighter than the annulus.
Prepare Ag/Cl electrodes using a 208 µm-thick silver wire and bleach in sodium hypochlorite for over 1 minute.
Place the Ag/Cl electrodes into each side of the chamber deep enough to be dipped into buffer solution.
Connect the electrodes to the microelectrode amplifier.
Apply a ±10 mV triangular waveform across the membrane using electrophysiology software.
Set applying voltage by clicking the arrows indicated on V_clamp (mV).
Record electrical properties of the membrane by clicking the record button (red dot icon) until a uniform square wave is observed.
Quit recording by clicking the black square icon.
Apply 100 mV across the membrane at a sample rate of 5 kHz to measure holding potential of the membrane.
Set applying voltage by clicking the arrows indicated on V_clamp (mV).
Record the electrical properties of the gA incorporation by clicking the record button (red dot icon).
Proceed the recording until current jumps are observed.
Quit the recording by clicking the black square icon.
Filter the data with a low-pass Bessel filter at 100 Hz using an electrophysiology software.
Observe current jumps in the filtered holding potential data to verify gA incorporation.
